perspective:
**Vincent Chinana’s available information:**

- Vincent knows he is a mechanic and that Patrick Guzman is his long-time friend, a construction worker. They met as teenagers and often collaborate on projects.
- At a local diner, Vincent discussed Patrick’s possible new construction venture. He heard Patrick say it seemed like a good opportunity to expand his business. Vincent told Patrick he had heard it was risky and asked if Patrick was sure. Patrick said it was worth the risk but he was still weighing options. Vincent expressed worry about financial security and suggested Patrick reconsider or delay until he had more information. Patrick thanked him and said he would think it over more.
- Over the next few days, Vincent noticed Patrick avoiding detailed discussion about the investment. At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent confronted him, saying he felt Patrick was not telling him everything. Patrick said it was complicated and he had not wanted to worry Vincent with details. Vincent said they needed to discuss it because he was Patrick’s friend and felt betrayed by the lack of transparency. Patrick apologized, said he should have been more open, and offered to sit down and explain everything.
- During a later detailed discussion at Vincent’s garage, Vincent learned the investment troubles were serious. He heard Patrick say it had been tough and that Patrick might lose a significant amount if it did not turn around soon. Vincent offered to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick thanked him and expressed gratitude for the support.
- A month later at a coffee shop, Vincent said the venture might actually turn a profit. He heard Patrick say it was starting to look up and that he was relieved they had stuck with it. Vincent apologized for doubting Patrick earlier and proposed a joint venture. Patrick agreed and said they should work out the details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent and Patrick met to draft a business plan for their joint venture. Vincent said their combined skills could make it a success. Patrick agreed and said he was excited. Vincent proposed starting the business plan and outlining every step carefully. Patrick agreed to cover all their bases and set it up for success.
- Vincent’s own actions include questioning Patrick’s plans, voicing concern, urging caution/delay, noticing Patrick’s avoidance, confronting him, offering a loan, apologizing for doubting him, proposing the joint venture, and beginning to plan it.
